rv.q: Allan isn’t simply performing magic, which he does to perfection, but is telling a story—one that proves sweetly sentimental and touching, infusing the proceedings with an emotionalism sorely lacking in most shows of its type.
I recommend it for families and for anyone who loves a Rubik's cube–filled trip down memory lane.
It sustains itself on healthy doses of surprises as its novelty fizzles out in Act 2, but parents and kids may spend worthwhile quality time at the sentimental show.
If you love illusions, you will not want to miss Jamie Allan’s AMAZE!
Themed in the 1980s, Amaze takes us back to Allan’s formative years, what lead him to become a magician. It’s charming. He’s charming.
This is a show that caters to everyone in the family, and it’s a show that certainly lives up to its ambitious title.
I did not leave with my jaw dropped but with a flicker of childhood wonder reignited, and a loving nod to the memories and mentors that taught me to find the extraordinary in the everyday.
Directed by Jonathan Goodwin, Jamie Allan’s Amaze is astonishing.
